index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a detailed block diagram of an FSA-based forward analysis model for predicting transmissibility from input metastructure images. It consists of two main parts: (a) the complete model architecture and (b) a detailed breakdown of the FEM-inspired Spatial Attention (FSA) module.

Part (a) shows the global layout of the forward model. The input image x enters the network and first undergoes normalization (Norm). This is followed by an N × Geometric feature extractor block, which contains a Geometric Attention (GA) module highlighted in orange. Inside GA, there are l × FSA heads (represented as grey boxes), each implementing the FSA mechanism. Outputs from these heads are concatenated and passed through a Conv2d projection layer (proj.), then a Dropout layer. The resulting feature map h is added to the original input x via a residual connection, forming the output x of this block. This output then passes through another Norm, Conv2d, and Dropout sequence before entering the Regression head.

The Regression head is enclosed in a dashed box and consists of a series of layers: Conv2d with ReLU activation followed by normalization, then Flatten combined with a Fully Connected (FC) layer using PReLU activation, followed by another FC layer with PReLU, and finally an FC layer with linear activation producing the output A (transmissibility). Material properties E, ρ, ν, d are fed into the final FC layer as additional inputs, indicated by a red box labeled 'Material properties'.

Part (b) provides a detailed view of the FSA module, titled 'FEM inspired Spatial Attention (FSA): Learning the neighborhood dependencies'. The input x is processed by a Conv2d layer with kernel size fα×α, producing feature map xf. This feature map is split into two paths: one undergoes Max pooling (F_max^s(xf)) and the other Avg pooling (F_avg^s(xf)). Each pooled output is multiplied by learnable weights w1 and w2 respectively, then concatenated. The concatenated result is passed through another Conv2d layer with kernel size fβ×β, generating xa^s. This is then passed through a sigmoid activation σ to produce a spatial attention map. Finally, the attention map is multiplied element-wise (matrix product ⊗) with the original feature map xf to produce the output xo. Mathematical equations below clarify: xa^s = fβ×β([w1F_avg^s(xf), w2F_max^s(xf)]) and xo = xf ⊗ σ(xa^s). Additional notation defines ⊗ as matrix product and fβ×β(.) as a Conv2d layer with kernel size β×β.

The diagram uses rectangular blocks for operations (e.g., Conv2d, Norm, Dropout), circles for activations (σ), and arrows to indicate data flow. The GA module is shaded orange, while individual FSA heads are grey. Text labels specify layer types, activations, and dimensions (e.g., ℝc×h×w). The overall structure follows a residual and attention-based deep learning architecture designed for geometrically-aware feature extraction.
